1.name: Paleozoic marine rocks, undivided, unit 4 (Western Sierra Nevada)
1.lithology: Major: argillite, quartzite, phyllite; Minor: mudstone, sandstone, chert; Incidental: schist, marble, conglomerate, sedimentary breccia, limestone, basalt
1.description: Undivided Paleozoic metasedimentary rocks. Includes slate, sandstone, shale, chert, conglomerate, limestone, dolomite, marble, phyllite, schist, hornfels, and quartzite
1.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 2.description: Mesozoic granite, quartz monzonite, granodiorite, and quartz diorite
2.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 3.name: Jurassic marine rocks, unit 1 (Western Sierra Nevada and Western Klamath Mountains)
3.lithology: Major: slate, graywacke; Minor: siltstone, conglomerate; Incidental: chert, volcanic, basalt

4.lithology: Major: sandstone, conglomerate; Incidental: sedimentary breccia, volcanic, mudstone, limestone, siltstone
4.description: Undivided Tertiary sandstone, shale, conglomerate, breccia, and ancient lake deposits.
4.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 5.name: Mesozoic volcanic rocks, unit 2 (Western Sierra Foothills and Western Klamath Mountains)
5.lithology: Major: mafic volcanic; Minor: felsic volcanic; Incidental: chert, sandstone, conglomerate
5.description: Undivided Mesozoic volcanic and metavolcanic rocks. Andesite and rhyolite flow rocks, greenstone, volcanic breccia and other pyroclastic rocks; in part strongly metamorphosed. Includes volcanic rocks of Franciscan Complex: basaltic pillow lava, diabase, greenstone, and minor pyroclastic rocks.
5.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 6.name: Ultramafic rocks, chiefly Mesozoic, unit 2 (Western Sierra Nevada and Klamath Mountains)
6.description: Ultramafic rocks, mostly serpentine. Minor peridotite, gabbro, and diabase. Chiefly Mesozoic unit 2
